nodes.label: Four-region resizable layout
nodes.rationale: Sizes persisted per breakpoint bucket via react-resizable-panels autoSaveId; at 1280-1599 Source becomes a Ctrl+E overlay splitting the centre horizontally rather than stealing tree width; phone is explicitly out of scope rather than half-supported.

nodes.label: Inspector section stack and per-document-kind registry
nodes.rationale: Everything about the selected node in one fixed place is the property beginners rely on most, and a registry lets XSD and Schematron swap sections in without a second layout implementation.

nodes.label: Tree row anatomy and density variables
nodes.rationale: Steal Chrome DevTools' Elements panel wholesale — badge chips, inline preview and a bottom breadcrumb are all proven at this density. The cardinality chip is literal ('2 of 0-∞') with tabular numerals so widths align, and indent guides for the focused node's ancestor chain are the cheapest orientation aid there is.

nodes.label: Namespace colouring from eight curated OKLCH hues
nodes.rationale: Free hue rotation produces low-contrast near-duplicates, so hash into a curated set. Colour tints only the prefix chip background and the prefix text is always shown, so colour is decoration and never information (WCAG 1.4.1). Unprefixed elements get a neutral grey chip so beginners learn a namespace is still in play.

nodes.label: Pre-emptive drag and drop, never post-hoc revert
nodes.rationale: Blockly and Scratch established that refusing at the boundary teaches the rule, whereas snap-back after acceptance teaches nothing. The full legal-drop set is computed once at drag start by asking the content-model engine which (parent, index) pairs accept the dragged QName.

nodes.label: Filtering narrows rather than highlights
nodes.rationale: Non-matching nodes hide but every match's full ancestor chain stays visible at 60% opacity so it is obvious they are context rather than matches; Escape restores the previous expansion state exactly, which means storing it before filtering.

nodes.label: Insert palette specification
nodes.rationale: Groups in fixed order, never re-sorting as you type. Fuzzy search matches documentation text as well as element names so typing 'price' surfaces an element named amt. The preview pane is where teaching actually happens, and when nothing is legal the empty state explains why rather than showing an empty list.

nodes.label: 'Add all required' is recursive and fills values
nodes.rationale: Every generated value is marked a placeholder, counted in an app-bar chip, steppable with F7 and cleared on first user edit. This turns 'valid but meaningless' into a guided to-do list, which is exactly what a beginner needs after a wizard drops them into a filled skeleton.

nodes.label: Smart paste helper sheet
nodes.rationale: Each ranked option is annotated with its validity consequence and the highest-validity option is default-selected. Converts the single most error-prone beginner action into a teaching moment while staying one keystroke for experts.

nodes.label: Keyboard map — the contract
nodes.rationale: Follows the WAI-ARIA APG tree pattern; Escape must never trap focus inside the tree. Insert is bound four ways (Ctrl+Space for IDE muscle memory, / for Notion muscle memory, +, Insert).

nodes.label: src/schema/describe.ts — the documentation guarantee
nodes.rationale: Priority order is xs:documentation in the user's language, then an xs:appinfo label, then a generated sentence. Every palette row, tooltip and Form-view hint calls this one function so no code path can render a blank description.

nodes.label: 'Why is this invalid?' — a fixed four-section popover
nodes.rationale: Same popover, same four sections, same order from every error badge. The raw cvc-* message must be available for people who will paste it into a search engine but must never be the primary text.

nodes.label: cvc-catalogue.ts and svrl-catalogue.ts message templates
nodes.rationale: Every cvc-* code maps to a template with typed slots (found, expected[], path); RedHat lemminx's code-action set is the best ready-made list of fix actions to mirror.

nodes.label: Form view — same model, no second state tree
nodes.rationale: Do not introduce react-hook-form or a JSON-Schema form library: the XML model is the single source of truth and every control dispatches the same commands as the tree, or the project is spent reconciling two states. Mixed-content nodes are not form-renderable and say so rather than showing a broken form.

nodes.label: Visible undo history panel
nodes.rationale: Labels are human sentences and clicking an entry time-travels and focuses affectedPath. Undo must always move focus and scroll to the affected node — silent undo is disorienting and is a top complaint about every editor in the prior art.

nodes.label: Onboarding empty states and three bundled examples
nodes.rationale: Empty states carry their weight: an empty tree with a schema attached shows a single ghost row '+ Add root element' so the very first action is one click. The third example fails one Schematron rule on open so the user sees error to explainer to quick fix to green within the first 60 seconds.

nodes.label: New-document wizard — five steps
nodes.rationale: Every step is back-navigable and the whole wizard is escapable to a blank-with-schema state. Never trap a user in a wizard they opened by accident. The optional step 4 collects top-level required values so the document is not born full of placeholders.

nodes.label: Expert mode differences table
nodes.rationale: Nothing is removed in either direction — an expert can still open the explainer, a beginner can still reach the raw source.

nodes.label: role="tree" with aria-activedescendant, rejecting treegrid
nodes.rationale: Treegrid's screen-reader support is inconsistent with dynamically-inserted rows and our rows have a variable number of cells, which breaks the grid's column model. activedescendant is forced by virtualization, which unmounts rows and would destroy DOM focus; VoiceOver handles it less well, compensated by an explicit polite live region.

nodes.label: One debounced polite live region and the delta-only rule
nodes.rationale: Validation announces the delta only, never the absolute count on every keystroke; one announce() helper debounced to at most one announcement per 1500ms so the region does not become noise, with role="alert" reserved for save-blocking errors.

nodes.label: Visual design tokens
nodes.rationale: Radix Colors 12-step OKLCH primitives behind semantic aliases, with dark mode using matching scales under identical alias names. Do not height-animate tree expand/collapse — animate only the twisty rotation, because height animation on a virtualized list janks badly. Nine custom glyphs cover XML semantics Lucide lacks.

nodes.label: XSD authoring mode UI
nodes.rationale: minOccurs/maxOccurs render as one editable 0..∞ control rather than two attributes buried in a list; the documentation card is editable because writing xs:documentation is the highest-leverage thing an XSD author can do for downstream users of this very editor. The Diagram tab is deferred since beginners cannot read that notation anyway.

nodes.label: Schematron authoring mode UI
nodes.rationale: The document is shallow so the Inspector swaps its attributes-first layout for a CodeMirror 6 XPath editor with namespace-aware completion from sch:ns. Pleasing reuse: Schematron is itself defined by a schema, so the same content-model engine drives this palette with no special-casing.

nodes.label: Prior art — steal precisely, and what to avoid
nodes.rationale: XMLSpy's Grid View table collapse, XXE's insert model, Oxygen's content-completion side pane, lemminx's code-action catalogue verbatim, nxml-mode's continuous validation. Avoided: Oxygen's mode dichotomy (users get stranded in a mode that cannot do what they want), XMLSpy's three stacked unexplained entry-helper panes (the anti-pattern this product exists to fix), and surfacing raw cvc-* strings as primary text.

nodes.label: Virtualization forces three design consequences
nodes.rationale: Fixed-height rows per density (so inline previews truncate rather than wrap), aria-activedescendant rather than DOM focus, and a guarded 'Expand all'. Plus: debounce selection-to-inspector at 60ms or held arrow keys stutter, and memoise palette candidates per (parent type, position) or they recompute on every filter keystroke.
